triples.rationale: Both accounts explicitly introduce an episode in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year: the image's construction and the king's account of prosperity before his dream. The shared dating is retained without adding an order of events within that year.
triples.source_text: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he said, “I was at peace in my house and prospering upon my throne.

target_units.text: In the eighteenth year, King Nebuchadnezzar, who administered cities and countries and all who inhabited the earth from India to Ethiopia, made a golden image, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of the enclosure in the country of Babylonia.

triples.rationale: Nebuchadnezzar again experiences a troubling dream that disturbs his peace. The earlier court narrative similarly begins with his dream and disturbed sleep before Daniel supplies its interpretation.
triples.source_text: I saw a dream and became apprehensive; fear fell upon me.

target_units.text: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, the king fell into visions and dreams and was disturbed in his dream, and his sleep left him.

triples.rationale: The great tree seen growing upon the earth is expressly identified in the interpretation as the king. The target supplies the image's stated referent.
triples.source_text: I was sleeping, and there was a tall tree growing upon the earth. Its appearance was great, and no other was like it.

target_units.text: You, O king, are the tree planted in the earth, whose appearance was great.

triples.rationale: The tree reaches heaven and the clouds. Daniel interprets that exalted height as the king's elevation above people and the pride of his heart against the Holy One.
triples.source_text: Its appearance was great: its top reached to heaven, and its mass to the clouds, filling what lay beneath heaven. The sun and moon dwelt in it and illuminated the whole earth.

target_units.text: The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.

triples.rationale: Birds nest in the tree whose branches shelter and sustain living creatures. The interpretation identifies its nesting birds with the peoples, languages and countries serving the king.
triples.source_text: Its branches were about thirty stadia long. All the wild animals of the earth found shade beneath it, and the birds of heaven nested in it. Its fruit was abundant and good, and it supplied all living creatures.

target_units.text: And all the birds of heaven nesting in it—the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all languages to the ends of the earth, and all countries—serve you.

triples.rationale: An angel is sent in strength from heaven. The interpretation explicitly recalls the angel's mission and the tree's cutting down as the great God's judgment upon the king.
triples.source_text: I was watching in my sleep, and an angel was sent in strength from heaven.

target_units.text: The vision you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord and commanded the tree’s removal and cutting down, means that the judgment of the great God will come upon you,

triples.rationale: The Most High commands the tree's removal and destruction. Daniel explains that command as divine judgment against the king, followed by custody and removal to a deserted place.
triples.source_text: He called out and said to it, ‘Cut it down and destroy it, for the Most High has commanded that it be uprooted and rendered useless.’

target_units.text: The vision you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord and commanded the tree’s removal and cutting down, means that the judgment of the great God will come upon you,
and the Most High and His angels are rushing against you.
They will lead you away into custody and send you to a deserted place.

triples.rationale: The instruction leaves one root in the earth. Daniel expressly explains the root's preservation as the keeping of the king's throne for him for a time.
triples.source_text: He spoke in this way: ‘Leave one root of it in the earth, so that it may graze on grass like an ox with the wild animals of the earth in the mountains;

target_units.text: The root of the tree that was left, since it was not uprooted, means that the place of your throne will be preserved for you for a time and an hour. Behold! They are preparing against you; they will scourge you and bring the judgments upon you.

triples.rationale: The vision assigns seven years of changed bodily existence and grazing. Nebuchadnezzar later reports seven years bound and fed grass like an ox, recounting that announced humiliation.
triples.source_text: let his body be changed by heaven’s dew, and let him graze with them for seven years,

target_units.text: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, was bound for seven years. They fed me grass like an ox, and I ate the earth’s greenery. After seven years I devoted my soul to supplication and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven; concerning my acts of ignorance I entreated the great God of gods.

triples.rationale: The judgment is to teach the king the heavenly Lord's authority over all things. His later thanksgiving credits God with creation, changing times and transferring kingdoms, expressing the lesson in his own royal confession.
triples.source_text: until he knows that the Lord of heaven has authority over everything in heaven and upon earth, and does among them whatever He wills.’

target_units.text: I give thanks to the Most High and praise Him who created heaven and earth, seas and rivers, and everything in them. I give thanks and praise, for He is God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. He performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, taking kingdoms from kings and appointing others in their place.

triples.rationale: The vision describes the fallen figure eating grass and being held in bonds. Nebuchadnezzar later reports being bound and fed grass like an ox for seven years, corresponding to those particular conditions.
triples.source_text: Before me it was cut down in one day, and its destruction came within one hour of the day. Its branches were given to every wind; it was dragged away and thrown down. It ate the grass of the earth with the wild animals of the earth, was handed over to custody, and was bound by them in fetters and bronze handcuffs. I was greatly astonished at all this, and sleep departed from my eyes.

target_units.text: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, was bound for seven years. They fed me grass like an ox, and I ate the earth’s greenery. After seven years I devoted my soul to supplication and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven; concerning my acts of ignorance I entreated the great God of gods.

triples.rationale: Daniel is summoned as chief of the learned experts and interpreter of dreams. The earlier narrative records his appointment as ruler and leader of Babylon's learned men after the first royal dream.
triples.source_text: In the morning I rose from my bed and called Daniel, chief of the learned experts and leader of those who judge dreams. I recounted the dream to him, and he explained its entire interpretation to me.

target_units.text: Then King Nebuchadnezzar exalted Daniel, gave him many great gifts, placed him over Babylonia’s affairs, and appointed him ruler and leader of all Babylonia’s learned men.

triples.rationale: Daniel's astonishment and changed appearance accompany the interpretation of the king's dream. At the end of his own beast vision, he again reports overwhelming astonishment and a changed condition.
triples.source_text: Daniel was greatly astonished, and apprehension pressed upon him. Frightened, seized with trembling, and changed in appearance, he shook his head and remained astonished for an hour. He answered me in a gentle voice, ‘O king, may this dream come upon those who hate you and its interpretation upon your enemies!

target_units.text: Until the account ended, I, Daniel, was greatly overcome with astonishment; my condition changed, and I fixed the matter in my heart.”

triples.rationale: Daniel identifies the king as the great tree planted in the earth, explicitly returning to the image first described in the dream.
triples.source_text: You, O king, are the tree planted in the earth, whose appearance was great.

target_units.text: I was sleeping, and there was a tall tree growing upon the earth. Its appearance was great, and no other was like it.

triples.rationale: The peoples and countries serving the king explain the birds nesting in the great tree, whose branches and fruit shelter and sustain living creatures in the dream.
triples.source_text: And all the birds of heaven nesting in it—the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all languages to the ends of the earth, and all countries—serve you.

target_units.text: Its branches were about thirty stadia long. All the wild animals of the earth found shade beneath it, and the birds of heaven nested in it. Its fruit was abundant and good, and it supplied all living creatures.

triples.rationale: The interpretation repeats the tree's reaching heaven and the clouds and explains it through the king's elevation and proud heart. The height of the image receives its explicit royal meaning.
triples.source_text: The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.

target_units.text: Its appearance was great: its top reached to heaven, and its mass to the clouds, filling what lay beneath heaven. The sun and moon dwelt in it and illuminated the whole earth.

triples.rationale: Daniel connects the king's destruction of God's house with the consecrated people's sins. Chronicles similarly narrates the people's desecration and rejection of God's messengers before the Chaldean assault burns the Lord's house.
triples.source_text: The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.

target_units.text: All the distinguished men of Judah, the priests, and the people of the land multiplied breaches of faith in the nations’ abominations and defiled the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.
The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

He brought against them a king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Zedekiah. They had no mercy on their virgins and carried away their elders. He handed everything into their hands.
All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and the magnates—he brought everything into Babylon.
He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.

triples.rationale: The interpretation explicitly recalls the angel sent in strength and the command to cut down the tree, identifying that action as divine judgment against the king.
triples.source_text: The vision you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord and commanded the tree’s removal and cutting down, means that the judgment of the great God will come upon you,

target_units.text: I was watching in my sleep, and an angel was sent in strength from heaven.
He called out and said to it, ‘Cut it down and destroy it, for the Most High has commanded that it be uprooted and rendered useless.’

triples.rationale: The explanation describes the Most High and His angels rushing against the king. The dream had portrayed an angel sent from heaven announcing the Most High's command against the tree representing him.
triples.source_text: and the Most High and His angels are rushing against you.

target_units.text: I was watching in my sleep, and an angel was sent in strength from heaven.

triples.rationale: The interpretation predicts the king's custody. He later describes himself as bound for seven years and fed grass, reporting the announced loss of royal freedom.
triples.source_text: They will lead you away into custody and send you to a deserted place.

target_units.text: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, was bound for seven years. They fed me grass like an ox, and I ate the earth’s greenery. After seven years I devoted my soul to supplication and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven; concerning my acts of ignorance I entreated the great God of gods.

triples.rationale: The surviving root means the king's throne is kept for him. The later restoration of his kingdom and glory records the outcome corresponding to that assurance.
triples.source_text: The root of the tree that was left, since it was not uprooted, means that the place of your throne will be preserved for you for a time and an hour. Behold! They are preparing against you; they will scourge you and bring the judgments upon you.

target_units.text: At that time my kingdom was restored to me and my glory returned to me.

triples.rationale: Daniel advises the king to redeem his injustices by almsgiving while seeking mercy. Sirach expressly compares almsgiving's atonement for sins with water extinguishing fire, joining the same act with the treatment of sin.
triples.source_text: The Lord lives in heaven, and His authority is over all the earth. Entreat Him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices by almsgiving, so that gentleness may be granted you, you may have many days upon your royal throne, and He may not destroy you. Love these words, for my word is accurate and your time is full.’”

target_units.text: Water will extinguish a blazing fire, and almsgiving will atone for sins.

triples.rationale: Nebuchadnezzar keeps the vision's judgment in his heart after hearing it. Daniel later says he fixed the matter of his own vision in his heart; both accounts conclude the hearing of a troubling revelation with inward retention.
triples.source_text: At the completion of the words, Nebuchadnezzar, when he heard the judgment of the vision, kept the words in his heart.

target_units.text: Until the account ended, I, Daniel, was greatly overcome with astonishment; my condition changed, and I fixed the matter in my heart.”

triples.relationship: narrative illustration of a wisdom warning
triples.rationale: The king boasts of Babylon as the product of his might and glory immediately before judgment removes his authority. Proverbs warns that insolence precedes ruin and commends humility instead, matching the movement from royal self-exaltation to downfall.
triples.source_text: He spoke and said, “This is great Babylon, which I built, and it will be called the house of my kingship through the strength of my might, for the honor of my glory.”

target_units.text: Insolence leads before ruin, and evil-mindedness before a fall.
Better a gentle-tempered person with humility than one who divides spoils with the insolent.

triples.rationale: The heavenly sentence transfers Nebuchadnezzar's kingdom and says God gives kingship to whomever He wishes. Daniel's earlier praise had expressly described God transferring and appointing kings.
triples.source_text: At the completion of his word, he heard a voice from heaven: “To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: Babylon’s kingdom has been taken from you and is given to another, a despised man in your house. Behold! I appoint him over your kingdom; he will take your authority, glory, and luxury, so that you may recognize that the God of heaven has authority over human kingship and will give it to whomever He wishes. By sunrise another king will rejoice in your house and take possession of your glory, strength, and authority.

target_units.text: He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,

triples.rationale: The angel announces the restoration of kingship after the seven years. Daniel's earlier explanation of the preserved root had said that the place of the king's throne would be kept for him.

triples.source_text: I give thanks to the Most High and praise Him who created heaven and earth, seas and rivers, and everything in them. I give thanks and praise, for He is God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. He performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, taking kingdoms from kings and appointing others in their place.

triples.relationship: exclusive divine power over life and death
triples.rationale: Nebuchadnezzar contrasts the powerless national gods with the God of heaven, who can kill and make alive. Deuteronomy likewise joins God's uniqueness with His power to put to death and make alive.
triples.source_text: From now on I will worship Him. Trembling has seized me through fear of Him, and I praise all His holy ones. For the gods of the nations have no strength in themselves to transfer one king’s kingdom to another king, to kill and make alive, to perform signs and great and fearsome wonders, or to change exceedingly great affairs, as the God of heaven has done in me, changing great affairs concerning me. Throughout all the days of my reign I will offer sacrifices to the Most High on behalf of my soul, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. I will do what is acceptable before Him—I and my people, my nation and my countries under my authority. Whoever has spoken against the God of heaven, and whoever is caught speaking anything against Him, I will condemn to death.”

target_units.text: See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.

triples.rationale: The king's circular letter thanks God for returning his throne, authority and greatness. The preceding narrative had reported the restoration of his kingdom and glory, which the letter now proclaims publicly.
triples.source_text: King Nebuchadnezzar wrote a circular letter to all the nations in every place, to the countries and all languages dwelling in every country, from generation to generation: “Praise the Lord, the God of heaven, and gloriously bring Him sacrifice and offering. I, king of kings, gloriously give thanks to Him, because He has dealt with me in this way: on that very day He seated me upon my throne; I regained my authority and my kingdom among my people, and my greatness was restored to me.”

target_units.text: At that time my kingdom was restored to me and my glory returned to me.

triples.rationale: Nebuchadnezzar addresses all nations and languages about God's wonders and enduring authority. Darius later writes to the same broad kinds of audience, calling them to worship the enduring God who rescued Daniel.
triples.source_text: “King Nebuchadnezzar to all nations, all countries, and all who dwell in them: May peace be multiplied to you at every time. Now I will explain to you the deeds that the great God has done with me. It pleased me to demonstrate to you and to your learned experts that there is a God, and His wonders are great; His kingship is an everlasting kingship, His authority from generation to generation.” He sent letters concerning everything that had happened to him in his kingdom to all the nations under his kingship.

target_units.text: Then Darius wrote to all nations, countries, and languages dwelling throughout his whole land, saying:
“Let all people in my kingdom bow to and worship Daniel’s God, for He is God who endures and lives from generation to generation for ever.
I, Darius, will bow to Him and serve Him all my days, for handmade idols cannot save as Daniel’s God redeemed Daniel.”

triples.rationale: The preface anticipates fingers writing on the plaster wall opposite the lamp during Baltasar's banquet. The narrative reports that same writing scene in its own sequence; the preface's additional details are retained rather than merged into the verse.
triples.source_text: King Baltasar held a great reception on the day of the dedication of his royal buildings and invited two thousand men from among his magnates. On that day Baltasar, elated by wine and boasting, praised all the nations’ cast and carved gods in his place, but gave no praise to God Most High. That very night fingers like a human’s came out and inscribed on the plaster of his house’s wall, opposite the lamp, “Mane, Phares, Thekel.” Their interpretation is: Mane, “It has been numbered”; Phares, “It has been taken away”; Thekel, “It has been weighed.”

target_units.text: At that very hour fingers like those of a human hand came out and wrote on the plaster of his house’s wall, opposite the light and before King Baltasar. He saw a hand writing.

target_units.text: The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands.
Nor is He served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything.
From one He made every nation of humanity to live upon the whole face of the earth, determining their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
so that they might seek God, if perhaps they might feel their way toward Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are His offspring.’
Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the divine nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human art and thought.

2 Chronicles 36:11.text: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles 36:13.text: in breaking his obligations to King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He hardened his neck and strengthened his heart so as not to return to the Lord God of Israel.

2 Chronicles 36:14.text: All the distinguished men of Judah, the priests, and the people of the land multiplied breaches of faith in the nations’ abominations and defiled the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles 36:15.text: The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.

2 Chronicles 36:16.text: They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

2 Chronicles 36:17.text: He brought against them a king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Zedekiah. They had no mercy on their virgins and carried away their elders. He handed everything into their hands.

2 Chronicles 36:18.text: All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and the magnates—he brought everything into Babylon.

2 Chronicles 36:19.text: He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.

2 Chronicles 36:20.text: He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,

2 Chronicles 36:21.text: to fulfill the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land accepted its Sabbaths, to keep Sabbath. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to complete seventy years.

2 Chronicles 36:22.text: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, after the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth had been fulfilled, the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians. He ordered a proclamation throughout his kingdom in writing, saying,

2 Chronicles 36:23.text: “Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has commanded me to build Him a house in Jerusalem in Judea. Who among you is of all His people? His God shall be with him, and let him go up.”

Acts 5:27.text: They brought them and made them stand before the council. The high priest questioned them,

Acts 5:28.text: saying, “Did we not strictly command you not to teach in this name? Yet look—you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.”

Acts 5:29.text: Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than human beings.

Acts 7:20.text: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful before God. He was brought up for three months in his father’s house.

Acts 7:21.text: When he was exposed, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up and brought him up as her own son.

Acts 7:22.text: Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in his words and deeds.

Acts 14:8.text: In Lystra a man was sitting who had no strength in his feet, unable to walk from his mother’s womb; he had never walked.

Acts 14:9.text: He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be made well,

Acts 14:10.text: and said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” He leaped up and began walking.

Acts 14:11.text: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voice, saying in Lycaonian, “The gods have come down to us in human likeness.”

Acts 14:12.text: They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the leading speaker.

Acts 14:13.text: The priest of Zeus, whose shrine was before the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.

Acts 14:14.text: When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out

Acts 14:15.text: and saying, “Men, why are you doing these things? We too are human beings, of the same nature as you. We proclaim good news to you: turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them.

Acts 14:16.text: In past generations He allowed all the nations to go their own ways.

Acts 14:17.text: Yet He did not leave Himself without witness in doing good, giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

Acts 14:18.text: Even by saying these things, they scarcely stopped the crowds from sacrificing to them.

Acts 16:22.text: The crowd joined the attack against them. The magistrates tore off their garments and ordered them to be beaten with rods.

Acts 16:23.text: After inflicting many blows on them, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to keep them securely.

Acts 16:24.text: Having received such an order, he put them in the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.

Acts 16:25.text: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, while the prisoners listened to them.

Acts 16:26.text: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the jail’s foundations were shaken. At once all the doors opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.

Acts 17:22.text: Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I perceive that in every respect you are very religious.

Acts 17:23.text: For as I passed through and observed your objects of worship, I also found an altar inscribed, ‘To an unknown god.’ What you worship without knowing, this I proclaim to you.

Acts 17:24.text: The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands.

Acts 17:25.text: Nor is He served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything.

Acts 17:26.text: From one He made every nation of humanity to live upon the whole face of the earth, determining their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,

Acts 17:27.text: so that they might seek God, if perhaps they might feel their way toward Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

Acts 17:28.text: For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are His offspring.’

Acts 17:29.text: Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the divine nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human art and thought.

Daniel 1:1.text: In the third year of King Joakim of Judea, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon arrived at Jerusalem and besieged it.

Daniel 1:2.text: The Lord handed the city into his hands, together with Joakim king of Judea and a portion of the Lord’s sacred vessels. He carried them away to Babylon and deposited them in his idol-temple.

Daniel 1:3.text: The king told Abiesdri, his chief eunuch, to bring him some of the sons of Israel’s magnates, of the royal family and of the chosen men:

Daniel 1:4.text: young men without blemish, handsome, knowledgeable in every kind of wisdom, literate, intelligent, wise, and strong enough to be in the king’s house, and to teach them letters and the Chaldean tongue,

Daniel 1:5.text: and to give them a ration from the king’s house each day, from the royal table and the wine the king drank, and to educate them for three years and place some of them before the king.

Daniel 1:6.text: Among the lineage of Israel’s sons from Judea were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

Daniel 1:7.text: The chief eunuch assigned them names: Daniel, Baltasar; Hananiah, Sedrach; Mishael, Misach; and Azariah, Abdenago.

Daniel 1:8.text: Daniel considered in his heart how he might avoid being polluted by the king’s dinner and the wine he drank, and petitioned the chief eunuch that he might not be contaminated.

Daniel 1:9.text: The Lord gave Daniel honor and favor before the chief eunuch.

Daniel 1:10.text: The chief eunuch said to Daniel, “I am anxious about my lord the king, who prescribed your food and drink, lest he see your faces drawn and weak beside the foreign youths being reared with you, and I risk my own neck.”

Daniel 1:11.text: Daniel said to Abiesdri, appointed chief eunuch over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

Daniel 1:12.text: “Test your servants for ten days, and let us be given legumes from the earth to eat, and water to drink.

Daniel 1:13.text: If our appearance looks drawn beside the other young men eating the royal dinner, then deal with your servants however you wish.”

Daniel 1:14.text: He dealt with them in this manner and tested them for ten days.

Daniel 1:15.text: After ten days their appearance was good and their bodily condition better than the other young men eating the royal dinner.

Daniel 1:16.text: Abiesdri kept removing their dinner and wine and giving them legumes in exchange.

Daniel 1:17.text: The Lord gave the young men knowledge, understanding, and practical wisdom in every literary skill; to Daniel He gave understanding in every utterance, vision, dreams, and all wisdom.

Daniel 1:18.text: After these days the king ordered them brought in, and the chief eunuch brought them before King Nebuchadnezzar.

Daniel 1:19.text: The king conversed with them, and among the wise no one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They remained beside the king.

Daniel 1:20.text: In every matter of discourse, understanding, and education about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times wiser than the learned experts and philosophers throughout his kingdom. The king honored them, appointed them rulers, and declared them wiser than all his own men in affairs throughout his land and kingdom.

Daniel 1:21.text: Daniel remained until the first year of the reign of Cyrus king of the Persians.

Daniel 2:1.text: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, the king fell into visions and dreams and was disturbed in his dream, and his sleep left him.

Daniel 2:2.text: The king ordered the incantation-singers, magi, and sorcerers of the Chaldeans brought in to report his dreams to him. They arrived and stood beside the king.

Daniel 2:3.text: The king said to them, “I have seen a dream, and my spirit was stirred; therefore I wish to understand the dream.”

Daniel 2:4.text: The Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language: “My lord king, live for ever! Report your dream to your servants, and we will explain its interpretation to you.”

Daniel 2:5.text: The king answered the Chaldeans, “Unless you truthfully report the dream to me and disclose its interpretation, you will be made a public example, and your possessions will be taken into the royal treasury.

Daniel 2:6.text: But if you make the dream clear to me and report its interpretation, you will receive gifts of every kind and be honored by me. Disclose the dream to me and interpret it.”

Daniel 2:7.text: They answered a second time, “O king, state the vision, and your servants will interpret accordingly.”

Daniel 2:8.text: The king said to them, “I know for certain that you are buying time, since you have seen that the matter has departed from me. As I have commanded, so it will be.

Daniel 2:9.text: Unless you truthfully report the dream and disclose its interpretation, you will meet death. You have agreed together to speak false words before me until the time changes. Now, if you tell me what I saw during the night, I will know that you can also disclose its interpretation.”

Daniel 2:10.text: The Chaldeans answered before the king, “No one on earth can tell the king what he has seen, as you ask. No king and no ruler asks such a thing of any wise man, magus, or Chaldean.

Daniel 2:11.text: The matter you seek, O king, is weighty and extraordinary. No one can disclose these things to the king except perhaps an angel, whose dwelling is not with any flesh. Therefore it cannot happen as you suppose.”

Daniel 2:12.text: Then the king became gloomy and deeply grieved and ordered all the wise men of Babylonia brought out.

Daniel 2:13.text: It was decreed that all should be killed, and Daniel and everyone with him were sought so that they might perish together.

Daniel 2:14.text: Then Daniel shared his counsel and judgment with Arioch, the king’s chief cook, who had been ordered to bring out Babylonia’s learned men,

Daniel 2:15.text: and questioned him, saying, “On what matter is such a bitter decree being issued by the king?” Then Arioch explained the command to Daniel.

Daniel 2:16.text: Daniel quickly went in to the king and petitioned for time from the king, so that he might disclose everything before him.

Daniel 2:17.text: Then Daniel went to his house and explained everything to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

Daniel 2:18.text: He called for fasting and supplication and for help to be sought from the Lord Most High concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and those with him would not be handed over to destruction with Babylon’s learned men.

Daniel 2:19.text: Then, in a vision that very night, the king’s mystery was plainly revealed to Daniel. Daniel blessed the Lord Most High,

Daniel 2:20.text: and cried out, “The name of the great Lord will be blessed for ever, because wisdom and majesty belong to Him.

Daniel 2:21.text: He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,

Daniel 2:22.text: reveals deep and dark things, knows what is in darkness and what is in light, and with Him is a dwelling.

Daniel 2:23.text: To Thee, Lord of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because Thou hast given me wisdom and prudence. Now Thou hast shown me everything I requested, to disclose these things to the king.”

Daniel 2:24.text: Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to kill all Babylonia’s learned men, and said, “Do not destroy Babylonia’s learned men. Bring me to the king, and I will disclose every detail to him.”

Daniel 2:25.text: Then Arioch urgently brought Daniel to the king and said, “I have found a wise man from the captivity of the sons of Judea who will disclose every detail to the king.”

Daniel 2:26.text: The king answered Daniel, who was called Baltasar in Chaldean, “Will you be able to disclose to me the vision I saw and its interpretation?”

Daniel 2:27.text: Daniel spoke aloud before the king, “Disclosure of the mystery the king saw does not belong to wise men, sorcerers, incantation-singers, or gazarenes,

Daniel 2:28.text: but there is a God in heaven who uncovers mysteries, who has disclosed to King Nebuchadnezzar what must happen in the last days. O king, live for ever! This is the dream and the vision of your head upon your bed:

Daniel 2:29.text: You, O king, reclining upon your bed, saw everything that must happen in the last days, and the Revealer of mysteries disclosed to you what must happen.

Daniel 2:30.text: This mystery was revealed to me because of no wisdom in me beyond all people; rather, so that it might be disclosed to the king, what you conceived in your heart was made known to me.

Daniel 2:31.text: You, O king, saw a single image. That image was exceedingly large, its appearance was extraordinary as it stood before you, and the image’s appearance was frightening.

Daniel 2:32.text: Its head was good gold, its chest and arms silver, and its belly and thighs bronze,

Daniel 2:33.text: its legs iron, and its feet partly iron and partly earthenware.

Daniel 2:34.text: You watched until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands. It struck the image on its feet of iron and earthenware and ground them down.

Daniel 2:35.text: Then the iron, earthenware, bronze, silver, and gold were ground fine together, becoming finer than chaff on a threshing floor. The wind scattered them so that nothing remained of them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain and struck the whole earth.

Daniel 2:36.text: This was the vision; now we will state its interpretation before the king.

Daniel 2:37.text: You, O king, are king of kings, and the Lord of heaven has given you rule, kingdom, strength, honor, and glory.

Daniel 2:38.text: Throughout the inhabited world He has handed over into your hands human beings, wild beasts, birds of heaven, and fish of the sea, to rule them all. You are the golden head.

Daniel 2:39.text: After you a kingdom lesser than you will arise, and another, a third kingdom of bronze, which will rule the whole earth.

Daniel 2:40.text: A fourth kingdom will be strong like iron that subdues everything and cuts down every tree, and the whole earth will be shaken.

Daniel 2:41.text: As you saw its feet partly potter’s earthenware and partly iron, another kingdom, divided in two, will be within it, just as you saw iron mixed with clay earthenware.

Daniel 2:42.text: The toes of the feet were partly iron and partly earthenware; part of the kingdom will be strong and part shattered.

Daniel 2:43.text: As you saw iron mixed with clay earthenware, they will be mingled in human generation, but will neither agree nor have goodwill toward one another, just as iron cannot blend with earthenware.

Daniel 2:44.text: In the times of these kings the God of heaven will establish another kingdom, which will exist for ever and will not be destroyed. This kingdom will not leave another nation; it will strike and obliterate these kingdoms and will itself stand for ever,

Daniel 2:45.text: just as you saw a stone cut from a mountain without hands, pounding together the earthenware, iron, bronze, silver, and gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen in the last days. The vision is exact, and its interpretation trustworthy.”

Daniel 2:46.text: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell face down on the ground and prostrated himself before Daniel. He ordered sacrifices and libations made to him.

Daniel 2:47.text: The king spoke aloud to Daniel, “Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, the One who alone brings hidden mysteries to light, because you have been able to disclose this mystery.”

Daniel 2:48.text: Then King Nebuchadnezzar exalted Daniel, gave him many great gifts, placed him over Babylonia’s affairs, and appointed him ruler and leader of all Babylonia’s learned men.

Daniel 2:49.text: Daniel petitioned the king that Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago be appointed over Babylonia’s affairs. Daniel remained in the royal court.

Daniel 3:1.text: In the eighteenth year, King Nebuchadnezzar, who administered cities and countries and all who inhabited the earth from India to Ethiopia, made a golden image, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of the enclosure in the country of Babylonia.

Daniel 3:2.text: Nebuchadnezzar, king of kings and lord of the whole inhabited world, sent to gather all the nations, tribes, and languages, satraps, generals, district governors, consuls, administrators, those holding authority in each country, and everyone throughout the inhabited world, to come to the dedication of the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Daniel 3:3.text: Those previously listed stood opposite the image.

Daniel 3:4.text: The herald proclaimed to the crowds, “You are commanded, nations and countries, peoples and languages:

Daniel 3:5.text: when you hear the sound of trumpet, panpipe, kithara, sambuca, psaltery, symphonia, and every kind of musical instrument, fall down and bow to the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.

Daniel 3:6.text: They will throw into the blazing furnace anyone who does not fall down and bow.”

Daniel 3:7.text: At that time, when all the nations heard the sound of the trumpet and every musical sound, all the nations, tribes, and languages fell down and bowed to the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up before him.

Daniel 3:8.text: At that time Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews.

Daniel 3:9.text: They spoke and said, “My lord king, live for ever!

Daniel 3:10.text: You, O king, commanded and decreed that everyone who hears the trumpet and every musical sound must fall down and bow to the golden image.

Daniel 3:11.text: Whoever does not fall down and bow will be thrown into the blazing furnace.

Daniel 3:12.text: There are certain Jewish men whom you appointed over the country of Babylonia—Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago. Those men have not feared your command; they have not served your idol or bowed to your golden image that you set up.”

Daniel 3:13.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar, angered with wrath, ordered Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago brought in. The men were brought to the king.

Daniel 3:14.text: When King Nebuchadnezzar saw them, he said to them, “Why, Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, do you not serve my gods or bow to the golden image I set up?

Daniel 3:15.text: Now, if you are ready, as soon as you hear the trumpet and every musical sound, to fall down and bow to the golden image I set up—but if not, know that unless you bow, you will immediately be thrown into the blazing furnace. What god will rescue you from my hands?”

Daniel 3:16.text: Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago answered King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, we have no need to answer you concerning this command.

Daniel 3:17.text: For there is a God in the heavens, our one Lord, whom we fear, who is able to rescue us from the furnace of fire; and from your hands, O king, He will rescue us.

Daniel 3:18.text: Then it will be plain to you that we neither serve your idol nor bow to your golden image that you set up.”

Daniel 3:19.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the appearance of his face changed. He ordered the furnace heated seven times beyond what it needed to be heated.

Daniel 3:20.text: He ordered the strongest men in his force to bind Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago hand and foot and throw them into the blazing furnace.

Daniel 3:21.text: Then those men were bound hand and foot, wearing their footwear and the tiaras on their heads, together with their clothing, and were thrown into the furnace.

Daniel 3:22.text: Because the king’s command was urgent and the furnace had been heated seven times beyond its earlier heat, the appointed men bound them hand and foot, brought them to the furnace, and threw them into it.

Daniel 3:23.text: The flame came out of the furnace and burned and killed the men who had bound Azariah and his companions; but they themselves were preserved.

Daniel 3:24.text: Thus Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael prayed and sang to the Lord when the king ordered them thrown into the furnace.

Daniel 3:25.text: Azariah stood and prayed in this manner. Opening his mouth, he gave thanks to the Lord together with his companions amid the fire, while the Chaldeans were fiercely stoking the furnace. They said:

Daniel 3:26.text: “Blessed art Thou, Lord, God of our fathers; Thy name is praised and glorified for ever.

Daniel 3:27.text: For Thou art righteous in everything Thou hast done to us; all Thy works are true, Thy ways upright, and all Thy judgments true.

Daniel 3:28.text: Thou hast carried out judgments of truth in everything Thou didst bring upon us and upon Thy holy city, our fathers’ Jerusalem. For in truth and judgment Thou didst all these things because of our sins.

Daniel 3:29.text: For we have sinned in everything and acted lawlessly by departing from Thee. We have sinned in everything and have not obeyed the commands of Thy law.

Daniel 3:30.text: We have neither kept nor done what Thou didst command us, so that it might go well with us.

Daniel 3:31.text: And now, everything Thou hast brought upon us and everything Thou hast done to us, Thou hast done in true judgment.

Daniel 3:32.text: Thou didst hand us over to our enemies, lawless and most hateful apostates, and to an unjust king, the most wicked in all the earth.

Daniel 3:33.text: Now we cannot open our mouths; shame and reproach have come upon Thy servants and those who revere Thee.

Daniel 3:34.text: Do not hand us over utterly, for Thy name’s sake; do not dissolve Thy covenant.

Daniel 3:35.text: Do not remove Thy mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham, beloved by Thee, and Isaac Thy servant, and Israel Thy holy one,

Daniel 3:36.text: as Thou didst speak to them, saying that Thou wouldst multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and the sand along the shore of the sea.

Daniel 3:37.text: For, Master, we have been diminished beyond all nations, and today we are lowly throughout the earth because of our sins.

Daniel 3:38.text: At this time there is no ruler or prophet or leader, no burnt offering or sacrifice or offering or incense, no place to offer produce before Thee and find mercy.

Daniel 3:39.text: But with a crushed soul and humbled spirit may we be accepted, as with burnt offerings of rams and bulls, and as with tens of thousands of fat lambs.

Daniel 3:40.text: So may our sacrifice be before Thee today; and be propitious—“behind Thee”; for there is no shame for those who trust in Thee; and bring to completion—“behind Thee.”

Daniel 3:41.text: Now we follow with our whole heart; we fear Thee and seek Thy face. Do not put us to shame,

Daniel 3:42.text: but deal with us according to Thy gentleness and the abundance of Thy mercy.

Daniel 3:43.text: Rescue us according to Thy wondrous deeds, and give glory to Thy name, Lord.

Daniel 3:44.text: May all who inflict evil on Thy servants be ashamed; may they be humiliated out of all their power, and may their strength be crushed.

Daniel 3:45.text: Let them know that Thou alone art Lord, God, glorious over the whole inhabited world.”

Daniel 3:46.text: The king’s servants who threw them in did not stop heating the furnace. When they threw the three together into the furnace, the furnace was sevenfold ablaze in its heat. When they threw them in, those casting them were above them, while others stoked beneath them with naphtha, tow, pitch, and vine brushwood.

Daniel 3:47.text: The flame spread above the furnace for forty-nine cubits.

Daniel 3:48.text: It spread out and burned those Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.

Daniel 3:49.text: An angel of the Lord descended into the furnace together with Azariah and his companions and shook the flame of fire out of the furnace.

Daniel 3:50.text: He made the middle of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze whistling through. The fire did not touch them at all; it neither distressed nor troubled them.

Daniel 3:51.text: Then the three took up the song as with one mouth, singing hymns, glorifying, blessing, and exalting God in the furnace, saying:

Daniel 3:52.text: “Blessed art Thou, Lord, God of our fathers, praised and highly exalted for ever. Blessed is the holy name of Thy glory, exceedingly praised and highly exalted through all ages.

Daniel 3:53.text: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy holy glory, exceedingly praised in hymns and exceedingly glorious for ever.

Daniel 3:54.text: Blessed art Thou upon the throne of Thy kingdom, praised in hymns and highly exalted for ever.

Daniel 3:55.text: Blessed art Thou who lookest upon the depths, seated upon cherubim, praised and glorified for ever.

Daniel 3:56.text: Blessed art Thou in the firmament, praised in hymns and glorified for ever.

Daniel 3:57.text: All works of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:58.text: Angels of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:59.text: Heavens, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:60.text: All waters above heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:61.text: All powers of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:62.text: Sun and moon, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:63.text: Stars of heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:64.text: All rain and dew, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:65.text: All winds, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:66.text: Fire and heat, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:67.text: Chill and cold, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:68.text: Dews and snowfalls, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:69.text: Ice and cold, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:70.text: Hoarfrost and snow, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:71.text: Nights and days, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:72.text: Light and darkness, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:73.text: Lightning and clouds, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:74.text: Let the earth bless the Lord; let her sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:75.text: Mountains and hills, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:76.text: All things growing upon the earth, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:77.text: Springs, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:78.text: Seas and rivers, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:79.text: Sea monsters and all things moving in the waters, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:80.text: All birds of heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:81.text: Four-footed creatures and wild animals of the earth, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:82.text: Sons of humankind, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:83.text: Israel, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:84.text: Priests, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:85.text: Servants, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:86.text: Spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:87.text: Holy ones and those humble in heart, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

Daniel 3:88.text: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever. For He rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hand of death; He delivered us from the midst of the burning flame and redeemed us from the fire.

Daniel 3:89.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures for ever.

Daniel 3:90.text: Bless, all who revere the God of gods; sing praise and give thanks, for His mercy endures for ever and for the age of ages.”

Daniel 3:91.text: When the king heard them singing and, standing, observed them alive, King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished, rose in haste, and said to his friends:

Daniel 3:92.text: “Behold! I see four men unbound, walking in the fire, and no harm has come upon them. The fourth has the likeness of an angel of God.”

Daniel 3:93.text: The king approached the door of the furnace blazing with fire and called them by name: “Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, servants of the Most High God of gods, come out of the fire!” Thus the men came out from the midst of the fire.

Daniel 3:94.text: The consuls, district governors, ancestral chiefs, and the king’s friends gathered. They observed those men: the fire had not touched their bodies, their hair had not burned, their trousers were unchanged, and there was no smell of fire on them.

Daniel 3:95.text: King Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, who sent His angel and saved His servants who hoped in Him. They rejected the king’s command and surrendered their bodies to burning so that they would neither serve nor bow to another god except their own God.

Daniel 3:96.text: Now I decree: from every nation, every tribe, and every language, whoever blasphemes the Lord, the God of Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, will be dismembered and his house confiscated, because there is no other god who can rescue like this.”

Daniel 3:97.text: Thus the king gave Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago authority over the whole country and appointed them rulers.

Daniel 4:4.text: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he said, “I was at peace in my house and prospering upon my throne.

Daniel 4:5.text: I saw a dream and became apprehensive; fear fell upon me.

Daniel 4:10.text: I was sleeping, and there was a tall tree growing upon the earth. Its appearance was great, and no other was like it.

Daniel 4:11.text: Its appearance was great: its top reached to heaven, and its mass to the clouds, filling what lay beneath heaven. The sun and moon dwelt in it and illuminated the whole earth.

Daniel 4:12.text: Its branches were about thirty stadia long. All the wild animals of the earth found shade beneath it, and the birds of heaven nested in it. Its fruit was abundant and good, and it supplied all living creatures.

Daniel 4:13.text: I was watching in my sleep, and an angel was sent in strength from heaven.

Daniel 4:14.text: He called out and said to it, ‘Cut it down and destroy it, for the Most High has commanded that it be uprooted and rendered useless.’

Daniel 4:15.text: He spoke in this way: ‘Leave one root of it in the earth, so that it may graze on grass like an ox with the wild animals of the earth in the mountains;

Daniel 4:16.text: let his body be changed by heaven’s dew, and let him graze with them for seven years,

Daniel 4:17.text: until he knows that the Lord of heaven has authority over everything in heaven and upon earth, and does among them whatever He wills.’

Daniel 4:17a.text: Before me it was cut down in one day, and its destruction came within one hour of the day. Its branches were given to every wind; it was dragged away and thrown down. It ate the grass of the earth with the wild animals of the earth, was handed over to custody, and was bound by them in fetters and bronze handcuffs. I was greatly astonished at all this, and sleep departed from my eyes.

Daniel 4:18.text: In the morning I rose from my bed and called Daniel, chief of the learned experts and leader of those who judge dreams. I recounted the dream to him, and he explained its entire interpretation to me.

Daniel 4:19.text: Daniel was greatly astonished, and apprehension pressed upon him. Frightened, seized with trembling, and changed in appearance, he shook his head and remained astonished for an hour. He answered me in a gentle voice, ‘O king, may this dream come upon those who hate you and its interpretation upon your enemies!

Daniel 4:20.text: You, O king, are the tree planted in the earth, whose appearance was great.

Daniel 4:21.text: And all the birds of heaven nesting in it—the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all languages to the ends of the earth, and all countries—serve you.

Daniel 4:22.text: The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.

Daniel 4:23.text: The vision you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord and commanded the tree’s removal and cutting down, means that the judgment of the great God will come upon you,

Daniel 4:24.text: and the Most High and His angels are rushing against you.

Daniel 4:25.text: They will lead you away into custody and send you to a deserted place.

Daniel 4:26.text: The root of the tree that was left, since it was not uprooted, means that the place of your throne will be preserved for you for a time and an hour. Behold! They are preparing against you; they will scourge you and bring the judgments upon you.

Daniel 4:27.text: The Lord lives in heaven, and His authority is over all the earth. Entreat Him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices by almsgiving, so that gentleness may be granted you, you may have many days upon your royal throne, and He may not destroy you. Love these words, for my word is accurate and your time is full.’”

Daniel 4:28.text: At the completion of the words, Nebuchadnezzar, when he heard the judgment of the vision, kept the words in his heart.

Daniel 4:29.text: After twelve months, the king was walking upon the city walls with all his glory and passing over its towers.

Daniel 4:30.text: He spoke and said, “This is great Babylon, which I built, and it will be called the house of my kingship through the strength of my might, for the honor of my glory.”

Daniel 4:31.text: At the completion of his word, he heard a voice from heaven: “To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: Babylon’s kingdom has been taken from you and is given to another, a despised man in your house. Behold! I appoint him over your kingdom; he will take your authority, glory, and luxury, so that you may recognize that the God of heaven has authority over human kingship and will give it to whomever He wishes. By sunrise another king will rejoice in your house and take possession of your glory, strength, and authority.

Daniel 4:32.text: The angels will pursue you for seven years. You will neither be seen nor speak with any human being. They will feed you grass like an ox, and your pasture will be the earth’s greenery. Behold! In place of your glory they will bind you, and another will have your luxurious house and your kingdom.

Daniel 4:33.text: By morning everything will be fulfilled upon you, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon; nothing of all this will fail.”

Daniel 4:33a.text: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, was bound for seven years. They fed me grass like an ox, and I ate the earth’s greenery. After seven years I devoted my soul to supplication and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven; concerning my acts of ignorance I entreated the great God of gods.

Daniel 4:33b.text: My hair became like an eagle’s wings, and my nails like a lion’s. My flesh and my heart were changed; I walked naked with the wild animals of the earth. I saw a dream, and apprehensions seized me. After a time a deep sleep took hold of me, and drowsiness fell upon me.

Daniel 4:34.text: At the completion of the seven years, the time of my release came. My sins and my acts of ignorance reached their full measure before the God of heaven. I entreated the great God of gods concerning my acts of ignorance, and an angel called to me from heaven, saying, ‘Nebuchadnezzar, serve the holy God of heaven and give glory to the Most High; the kingship of your nation is restored to you.’

Daniel 4:36.text: At that time my kingdom was restored to me and my glory returned to me.

Daniel 4:37.text: I give thanks to the Most High and praise Him who created heaven and earth, seas and rivers, and everything in them. I give thanks and praise, for He is God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. He performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, taking kingdoms from kings and appointing others in their place.

Daniel 4:37a.text: From now on I will worship Him. Trembling has seized me through fear of Him, and I praise all His holy ones. For the gods of the nations have no strength in themselves to transfer one king’s kingdom to another king, to kill and make alive, to perform signs and great and fearsome wonders, or to change exceedingly great affairs, as the God of heaven has done in me, changing great affairs concerning me. Throughout all the days of my reign I will offer sacrifices to the Most High on behalf of my soul, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. I will do what is acceptable before Him—I and my people, my nation and my countries under my authority. Whoever has spoken against the God of heaven, and whoever is caught speaking anything against Him, I will condemn to death.”

Daniel 4:37b.text: King Nebuchadnezzar wrote a circular letter to all the nations in every place, to the countries and all languages dwelling in every country, from generation to generation: “Praise the Lord, the God of heaven, and gloriously bring Him sacrifice and offering. I, king of kings, gloriously give thanks to Him, because He has dealt with me in this way: on that very day He seated me upon my throne; I regained my authority and my kingdom among my people, and my greatness was restored to me.”

Daniel 4:37c.text: “King Nebuchadnezzar to all nations, all countries, and all who dwell in them: May peace be multiplied to you at every time. Now I will explain to you the deeds that the great God has done with me. It pleased me to demonstrate to you and to your learned experts that there is a God, and His wonders are great; His kingship is an everlasting kingship, His authority from generation to generation.” He sent letters concerning everything that had happened to him in his kingdom to all the nations under his kingship.

Daniel 5:preface.text: King Baltasar held a great reception on the day of the dedication of his royal buildings and invited two thousand men from among his magnates. On that day Baltasar, elated by wine and boasting, praised all the nations’ cast and carved gods in his place, but gave no praise to God Most High. That very night fingers like a human’s came out and inscribed on the plaster of his house’s wall, opposite the lamp, “Mane, Phares, Thekel.” Their interpretation is: Mane, “It has been numbered”; Phares, “It has been taken away”; Thekel, “It has been weighed.”

Daniel 5:1.text: King Baltasar held a great banquet for his companions and drank wine.

Daniel 5:2.text: His heart was exalted, and he ordered the gold and silver vessels of God’s house that his father Nebuchadnezzar had brought from Jerusalem to be brought in, and wine poured in them for his companions.

Daniel 5:3.text: They were brought, and they drank from them,

Daniel 5:4.text: and blessed their handmade idols. But they did not bless the everlasting God, who had authority over their breath.

Daniel 5:5.text: At that very hour fingers like those of a human hand came out and wrote on the plaster of his house’s wall, opposite the light and before King Baltasar. He saw a hand writing.

Daniel 5:6.text: His appearance changed, and fears and apprehensions pressed upon him. The king hurried and rose to look at that writing, while his companions around him were boasting.

Daniel 5:7.text: The king cried out with a loud voice to summon the incantation-singers, sorcerers, Chaldeans, and gazarenes to report the writing’s interpretation. They came in to inspect the writing, but could not interpret it for the king. Then the king issued a decree: “Any man who explains the writing’s interpretation will be clothed in purple and have a gold necklace placed upon him, and he will be given authority over a third part of the kingdom.”

Daniel 5:8.text: The incantation-singers, sorcerers, and gazarenes came in, but no one could report the writing’s interpretation.

Daniel 5:9.text: Then the king summoned the queen about the sign and explained to her how great it was, and that no one could report the writing’s interpretation to the king.

Daniel 5:10.text: Then the queen mentioned to him Daniel, who was from the captivity of Judea,

Daniel 5:11.text: and said to the king, “The man was knowledgeable and wise, surpassing all Babylon’s wise men,

Daniel 5:12.text: and a holy spirit is in him. In the days of your father the king, he explained extraordinary interpretations to Nebuchadnezzar your father.”

Daniel 5:13.text: Then Daniel was brought before the king, and the king addressed him:

Daniel 5:16.text: “O Daniel, can you explain the writing’s interpretation to me? I will clothe you in purple and place a gold necklace upon you, and you will have authority over a third part of my kingdom.”

Daniel 5:17.text: Then Daniel stood opposite the writing and read it. He answered the king in this way: “This is the writing: ‘It has been numbered, it was reckoned, it has been taken away.’ The hand that wrote came to a stop. This is their interpretation:

Daniel 5:23.text: O king, you held a banquet for your friends and drank wine. The vessels of the living God’s house were brought to you, and you and your magnates drank from them and praised all the idols made by human hands. But you did not bless the living God. Your breath is in His hand, and He gave you your kingdom, yet you neither blessed Him nor offered Him praise.

Daniel 5:26–28.text: This is the writing’s interpretation: your time of kingship has been numbered; your kingdom is ending. Your kingdom has been cut short and brought to completion; it is given to the Medes and Persians.”

Daniel 5:29.text: Then King Baltasar clothed Daniel in purple, placed a gold necklace upon him, and gave him authority over a third part of his kingdom.

Daniel 5:30.text: The interpretation came upon King Baltasar; the kingship was taken from the Chaldeans and given to the Medes and Persians.

Daniel 6:1.text: Artaxerxes of the Medes received the kingdom. Darius was full of days and glorious in old age.

Daniel 6:2.text: He appointed one hundred twenty-seven satraps over his whole kingdom,

Daniel 6:3.text: and over them three men as their leaders. Daniel was one of the three men,

Daniel 6:4.text: having authority above everyone in the kingdom. Daniel was clothed in purple, great and glorious before King Darius, because he was distinguished, knowledgeable, and understanding, with a holy spirit in him, and prospered in the king’s affairs that he conducted. Then the king decided to appoint Daniel over his whole kingdom, along with the two men whom he had appointed with him and one hundred twenty-seven satraps.

Daniel 6:5.text: When the king decided to appoint Daniel over his whole kingdom, the two young men devised a plan and resolution together. Since they could find no sin or ignorant fault in Daniel of which they could accuse him before the king,

Daniel 6:6.text: they said, “Come, let us establish a restriction binding upon ourselves: no one is to make a request or offer a prayer to any god for thirty days, except to King Darius; otherwise he will die.” They intended to bring Daniel down before the king and have him thrown into the lions’ pit, for they knew that Daniel prayed and entreated the Lord his God three times a day.

Daniel 6:7.text: Then those men approached and said before the king:

Daniel 6:8.text: “We have established a restriction and decree: anyone who offers a prayer or makes any request to any god for thirty days, except to King Darius, will be thrown into the lions’ pit.”

Daniel 6:9.text: They asked the king to establish the restriction and not alter it, because they knew that Daniel prayed and entreated three times a day; they intended him to be brought down through the king and thrown into the lions’ pit.

Daniel 6:10.text: Thus King Darius established and ratified it.

Daniel 6:11.text: When Daniel learned of the restriction established against him, he opened windows in his upper room toward Jerusalem, fell upon his face three times a day as he had done before, and made supplication.

Daniel 6:12.text: They watched Daniel and caught him praying three times a day, every day.

Daniel 6:13.text: Then these men appealed to the king and said, “King Darius, did you not decree a restriction that no one should offer a prayer or make a request to any god for thirty days except to you, O king, otherwise he would be thrown into the lions’ pit?” The king answered them, “The statement is exact, and the restriction will remain.”

Daniel 6:13a.text: They said to him, “We adjure you by the decrees of the Medes and Persians: do not alter the command, show partiality, or diminish anything that has been stated; punish the man who has not kept this restriction.” He said, “I will do as you say; this is established with me.”

Daniel 6:14.text: They said, “Behold! We found Daniel your friend praying and seeking the face of his God three times a day.”

Daniel 6:15.text: The king, grieved, ordered Daniel thrown into the lions’ pit according to the restriction he had established against him. Then the king was deeply grieved over Daniel and tried to rescue him from the satraps’ hands until sunset,

Daniel 6:16.text: but could not rescue him from them.

Daniel 6:17.text: King Darius cried out and said to Daniel, “Your God, whom you worship continually three times a day, will rescue you from the lions’ power. Take courage until morning.”

Daniel 6:18.text: Then Daniel was thrown into the lions’ pit. A stone was brought and placed at the pit’s mouth, and the king sealed it with his own ring and his magnates’ rings, so that Daniel could not be taken away from them, nor could the king pull him up from the pit.

Daniel 6:19.text: Then the king returned to his royal residence and spent the night fasting, grieving over Daniel. Daniel’s God, taking care of him, shut the lions’ mouths, and they did not trouble Daniel.

Daniel 6:20.text: King Darius rose early in the morning, took the satraps with him, and went and stood at the mouth of the lions’ pit.

Daniel 6:21.text: Then the king called to Daniel with a loud voice and weeping: “O Daniel, are you perhaps alive? Has your God, whom you worship continually, saved you from the lions, so that they have not destroyed you?”

Daniel 6:22.text: Then Daniel answered with a loud voice and said, “O king, I am still alive,

Daniel 6:23.text: and God has saved me from the lions, because righteousness was found in me before Him. Before you also, O king, neither ignorant fault nor sin was found in me. Yet you listened to men who mislead kings and threw me into the lions’ pit for destruction.”

Daniel 6:24.text: Then all the forces assembled and saw Daniel, whom the lions had not troubled.

Daniel 6:25.text: Then those two men who had testified against Daniel, with their wives and children, were thrown to the lions. The lions killed them and crushed their bones.

Daniel 6:26.text: Then Darius wrote to all nations, countries, and languages dwelling throughout his whole land, saying:

Daniel 6:27.text: “Let all people in my kingdom bow to and worship Daniel’s God, for He is God who endures and lives from generation to generation for ever.

Daniel 6:28.text: I, Darius, will bow to Him and serve Him all my days, for handmade idols cannot save as Daniel’s God redeemed Daniel.”

Daniel 6:29.text: King Darius was gathered to his people, and Daniel was appointed in Darius’s reign. Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.

Daniel 7:1.text: In the first year of Baltasar’s reign over the country of Babylonia, Daniel saw a vision at his head upon his bed. Then Daniel wrote the vision he had seen in principal points:

Daniel 7:2.text: “Upon my bed I was watching in dreams by night, and there were four winds of heaven falling upon the great sea.

Daniel 7:3.text: Four beasts came up from the sea, each differing from the other.

Daniel 7:4.text: The first was like a lioness with wings like an eagle’s. I watched until her wings were plucked out, she was lifted from the earth and stood on human feet, and a human heart was given her.

Daniel 7:5.text: After her there was another beast with the likeness of a bear. It stood on one side and had three ribs in its mouth. He spoke in this way: ‘Rise, devour much flesh!’

Daniel 7:6.text: After this I watched another beast, like a leopard. Four wings stretched over it, and the beast had four heads; a tongue was given it.

Daniel 7:7.text: After this I watched in the night vision a fourth beast, fearsome, its terror surpassing in strength. It had great iron teeth, devoured and pounded, trampled all around with its feet, and acted differently from all the beasts before it. It had ten horns,

Daniel 7:8.text: and many plans were in its horns. Another single horn sprouted among them, small among its horns, and three of the earlier horns were withered through it. This horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and it made war against the holy ones.

Daniel 7:9.text: I watched until thrones were set in place and an Ancient of Days was seated, wearing a covering like snow, with the hair of His head like pure white wool. The throne was like a flame of fire,

Daniel 7:10.text: and a river of fire came out before Him. A thousand thousands attended Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood beside Him. A court sat, and books were opened.

Daniel 7:11.text: Then I watched the sound of the great words the horn was speaking. The beast was beaten to death, its body perished, and it was given over to burning fire.

Daniel 7:12.text: He removed those around it from their authority, and a span of life was given them for a time and a season.

Daniel 7:13.text: I watched in the night vision, and there, upon the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man was coming. He was present as an Ancient of Days, and those standing by were present with him.

Daniel 7:14.text: Authority was given him, and all the nations of the earth according to their families, and all glory, worshipped him. His authority is everlasting authority that will never be taken away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.

Daniel 7:15.text: I, Daniel, was disheartened by these things in the night vision,

Daniel 7:16.text: and approached one of those standing there, seeking exact understanding from him concerning all these things. He answered me and explained the judgment of the words:

Daniel 7:17.text: ‘These great beasts are four kingdoms that will perish from the earth.

Daniel 7:18.text: The holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and hold the kingdom for ever, for the age of ages.’

Daniel 7:19.text: Then I wanted exact understanding of the fourth beast, which destroyed everything and was exceedingly fearsome. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze, devouring everyone all around and trampling with its feet,

Daniel 7:20.text: and of its ten horns upon its head and the single other that sprouted, through which three fell out. That horn had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance surpassed the others.

Daniel 7:21.text: I observed that horn waging war against the holy ones and routing them,

Daniel 7:22.text: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High. The time was given, and the holy ones took possession of the kingship.

Daniel 7:23.text: I was told concerning the fourth beast that a fourth kingdom would be upon the earth, surpassing the whole earth, overturning it and grinding it down.

Daniel 7:24.text: As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.

Daniel 7:25.text: He will speak words against the Most High, wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and expect to alter seasons and law. Everything will be handed into his hands for a time, times, and half a time.

Daniel 7:26.text: The judgment will sit; they will destroy the authority and plan to defile and destroy completely.

Daniel 7:27.text: He gave the kingdom, authority, their greatness, and rule over all the kingdoms under heaven to a holy people of the Most High, to reign with everlasting kingship; all authorities will be subject to him and obey him.

Daniel 7:28.text: Until the account ended, I, Daniel, was greatly overcome with astonishment; my condition changed, and I fixed the matter in my heart.”

Daniel 8:1.text: In the third year of Baltasar’s reign came the vision that I, Daniel, saw after seeing the first one.

Daniel 8:2.text: I saw in the vision of my dream, while I was in the city of Susa in the country of Elymais, still beside the gate of Ailam,

Daniel 8:3.text: that, looking up, I saw a great ram standing opposite the gate. It had horns, one higher than the other, and the higher one was rising.

Daniel 8:4.text: After this I saw the ram charging eastward, northward, westward, and southward. No animals stood before it, and no one rescued from its hands. It did as it wished and was exalted.

Daniel 8:5.text: I was pondering, and a male goat came from the west over the earth’s surface without touching the earth. The goat had a single horn between its eyes.

Daniel 8:6.text: It came against the horned ram that I had seen standing beside the gate and ran at it in furious anger.

Daniel 8:7.text: I saw it approach the ram, become furious with it, strike it, and shatter its two horns. The ram no longer had strength to stand against the goat. It hurled the ram down upon the earth and crushed it, and no one could rescue the ram from the goat.

Daniel 8:8.text: The male goat grew exceedingly strong. When it became strong, its great horn was shattered, and four other horns rose behind it toward the four winds of heaven.
