Daniel 8:9.text: From one of them a single strong horn sprouted. It grew strong and struck toward the south, toward the east, and toward the north.

Daniel 8:10.text: It was raised as high as heaven’s stars, but was dashed to the earth from the stars and trampled by them,

Daniel 8:11.text: until the chief commander rescues the captivity. Because of him the ancient mountains were dashed down; their place and sacrifice were removed. He set it down upon the earth, and it prospered and came to pass, and the sanctuary will be made desolate.

Daniel 8:12.text: Sins came upon the sacrifice; righteousness was thrown down to the ground, and he acted and prospered.

Daniel 8:13.text: I heard another holy one speaking, and the other said to the speaking Phelmouni, “How long will the vision stand, and the sacrifice that was removed, and the sin of desolation that was given, and the holy places be made desolate for trampling?”

Daniel 8:14.text: He said to him, “Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; then the sanctuary will be cleansed.”

Daniel 8:15.text: As I, Daniel, watched the vision, I sought to understand, and there stood opposite me someone with a human appearance.

Daniel 8:16.text: I heard a human voice in the midst of Ulai, calling, “Gabriel, give that one understanding of the vision.” The man cried out and said, “The vision concerns that command.”

Daniel 8:17.text: He came and stood beside where I stood. As he came, I was disturbed and fell upon my face. He said to me, “Understand, son of man, for this vision is still for an appointed hour.”

Daniel 8:18.text: As he spoke with me, I fell asleep face down on the ground. He touched me and raised me on the spot,

Daniel 8:19.text: and said to me, “Behold! I am reporting what will happen at the end of the wrath to the sons of your people; it will still remain until the hours of the appointed time of completion.

Daniel 8:20.text: The ram you saw with the horns is the king of the Medes and Persians.

Daniel 8:21.text: The male goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king himself.

Daniel 8:22.text: As for the four horns that were shattered and rose behind it, four kings of his nation will arise, but not according to his strength.

Daniel 8:23.text: At the end of their kingship, when their sins reach fullness, a king with a shameless face who understands riddles will arise.

Daniel 8:24.text: His strength will be made firm, though not by his own strength. He will destroy astonishingly, prosper, and act; he will destroy rulers and a people of holy ones.

Daniel 8:25.text: His intent will be against the holy ones; falsehood will prosper in his hands, and his heart will be exalted. By deceit he will make many disappear, rise for the destruction of men, make a “gathering of a hand,” and sell.

Daniel 8:26.text: The evening-and-morning vision was found to be true. Now the vision is closed up, for it is still for many days.”

Daniel 8:27.text: I, Daniel, was weak for many days. Then I rose and again conducted royal affairs. I was undone by the vision, and there was no one who understood.

Daniel 9:1.text: In the first year under Darius son of Xerxes, from the Median family who ruled over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,

Daniel 9:2.text: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, considered in the books the number of years, when a command came to the land concerning Jeremiah the prophet, to bring Jerusalem’s reproach to its full term: seventy years.

Daniel 9:3.text: I set my face toward the Lord God to find prayer and mercy, with fasts, sackcloth, and ashes.

Daniel 9:4.text: I prayed to the Lord God and confessed, saying, “Behold, Lord, Thou art the great, strong, and fearsome God, keeping the covenant and mercy for those who love Thee and guard Thy commands:

Daniel 9:5.text: we have sinned, done wrong, acted impiously, fallen away, and transgressed Thy commandments and judgments,

Daniel 9:6.text: and have not listened to Thy servants the prophets, to what they spoke in Thy name to our kings, our rulers, our fathers, and every nation upon the earth.

Daniel 9:7.text: Righteousness belongs to Thee, Lord, but shame of face to us as on this day—to the people of Judah, those dwelling in Jerusalem, and all the people Israel, near and far, in all the countries where Thou didst scatter them because of the trespass they committed before Thee.

Daniel 9:8.text: Master, shame of face belongs to us, to our kings, rulers, and fathers, because we have sinned against Thee.

Daniel 9:9.text: To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy, for we have fallen away from Thee

Daniel 9:10.text: and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow Thy law that Thou didst set before Moses and us through Thy servants the prophets.

Daniel 9:11.text: All Israel abandoned Thy law and fell away, refusing to hear Thy voice. The curse and oath written in the law of Moses, God’s servant, came upon us, because we sinned against Him.

Daniel 9:12.text: He established for us His commands, all He spoke against us and against our judges, all Thou didst judge for us, bringing great calamities upon us, such as had not occurred under heaven as occurred in Jerusalem.

Daniel 9:13.text: According to what is written in Moses’ covenant, all the calamities came upon us. Yet we did not seek the face of the Lord our God by departing from our sins and understanding Thy righteousness, Lord.

Daniel 9:14.text: The Lord God kept watch over the calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in everything He may do, and we did not listen to His voice.

Daniel 9:15.text: Now, Master, Lord our God, who didst bring Thy people out of Egypt with Thine uplifted arm and didst make Thyself a name as on this day: we have sinned and acted in ignorance.

Daniel 9:16.text: Master, according to Thy righteousness, let Thy wrath and anger turn away from Thy city Jerusalem, Thy holy mountain. Because of our sins and our fathers’ acts of ignorance, Jerusalem and Thy people, Lord, are a reproach among all around us.

Daniel 9:17.text: Now, Master, hear Thy servant’s prayer and my supplications. Let Thy face look upon Thy desolate holy mountain, for Thy servants’ sake, Master.

Daniel 9:18.text: Attend with Thine ear, Lord, and hear me. Open Thine eyes and see our desolation and that of Thy city, over which Thy name has been called. For we make our supplication in our prayers before Thee because of Thy mercy, not our righteous deeds.

Daniel 9:19.text: Lord, be propitious! Lord, hear and act, and do not delay, for Thine own sake, Master, because Thy name has been called over Thy city Zion and Thy people Israel.”

Daniel 9:20.text: While I was speaking in prayer, confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and making supplication in prayers before the Lord my God and on behalf of our God’s holy mountain,

Daniel 9:21.text: while I was still speaking in my prayer, the man I had seen at first in my sleep, Gabriel, was carried swiftly and approached me at the hour of the evening sacrifice.

Daniel 9:22.text: He approached and spoke with me, saying, “Daniel, I have just come out to show you understanding.

Daniel 9:23.text: At the beginning of your supplication, a command went out from the Lord, and I came to explain it to you, because you are worthy of pity. Understand the command.

Daniel 9:24.text: Seventy weeks have been determined for your people and the city Zion: for sin to be brought to completion, injustices to become scarce, injustices to be wiped away, the vision to be understood, everlasting righteousness to be given, the vision to be fulfilled, and a holy of holies to be gladdened.

Daniel 9:25.text: You will know, understand, and rejoice. You will find commands to be answered, and you will build Jerusalem as a city for the Lord.

Daniel 9:26.text: After seven and seventy and sixty-two, an anointing will be removed and no longer exist. A kingdom of nations will destroy the city and sanctuary together with the anointed one. Its completion will come with wrath and last until the time of completion; it will be assailed by war.

Daniel 9:27.text: The covenant will prevail for many. It will return again and be rebuilt in breadth and length. At the completion of times, after seven and seventy periods and sixty-two years, until the time of the completion of war, desolation will be removed when the covenant grows strong for many weeks. At the end of the week the sacrifice and libation will be removed. Upon the temple will be an abomination of desolations until completion, and completion will be given upon the desolation.”

Daniel 10:1.text: In the first year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a command was shown to Daniel, whose name was called Baltasar. The vision and command were true, and the strong multitude will understand the command; I understood it in a vision.

Daniel 10:2.text: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks.

Daniel 10:3.text: I ate no desirable bread; meat and wine did not enter my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until I completed the three weeks of days.

Daniel 10:4.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,

Daniel 10:5.text: and I lifted my eyes and saw a man clothed in fine linen, with fine linen wrapped around his waist, and light coming from his middle.

Daniel 10:6.text: His body was like a tarshish stone, his face like a flash of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and feet like flashing bronze, and the sound of his speech like the sound of an uproar.

Daniel 10:7.text: I, Daniel, saw this great vision, but the men with me did not see it. Strong fear fell upon them, and they fled in haste.

Daniel 10:8.text: I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; a spirit turned upon me for destruction, and I had no strength.

Daniel 10:9.text: I did not hear the sound of his speech; I had fallen face down upon the earth.

Daniel 10:10.text: He brought a hand toward me and raised me upon my knees, upon the soles of my feet.

Daniel 10:11.text: He said to me, “Daniel, you are a man worthy of pity. Understand the commands I speak to you, and stand in your place, for I have just been sent to you.” As he spoke this command with me, I stood trembling.

Daniel 10:12.text: He said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel. From the first day you set your face to understand and humble yourself before the Lord your God, your word was heard, and I entered because of your word.

Daniel 10:13.text: The general of the king of the Persians stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the foremost rulers, came to help me, and I left him there with the general of the king of the Persians.”

Daniel 10:14.text: He said to me, “I came to show you what will meet your people in the latter days, for the vision is still for days to come.”

Daniel 10:15.text: As he spoke these commands with me, I set my face toward the earth and fell silent.

Daniel 10:16.text: Something like a human hand touched my lips. I opened my mouth, spoke, and said to the one standing opposite me, “My lord, something like a vision turned upon my side, upon me, and there was no strength in me.

Daniel 10:17.text: How can the servant speak with his lord? I have become weak; there is no strength in me, and no breath was left in me.”

Daniel 10:18.text: Again one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me,

Daniel 10:19.text: and said to me, “You are a man worthy of pity. Do not fear; be well. Take courage and be strong.” As he spoke with me, I became strong and said, “Let my lord speak, for he has strengthened me.”

Daniel 10:20.text: He said to me, “Do you know why I came to you? Now I will return to contend with the general of the king of the Persians. I was going out, and the general of the Greeks was coming in.

Daniel 10:21.text: I will indeed show you the first things in a record of truth. No one was helping with me concerning these except Michael the angel.”

Daniel 11:1.text: In the first year of King Cyrus, he told me to be strong and take courage.

Daniel 11:2.text: “Now I have come to show you the truth. Three kings have stood in opposition in Persia, and the fourth will become richer than all the others. When he grows strong through his wealth, he will rise against every king of the Greeks.

Daniel 11:3.text: A powerful king will arise, exercise great lordship, and do whatever he wishes.

Daniel 11:4.text: When he arises, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not according to his might or the lordship with which he ruled. His kingdom will be removed, and he will teach others these things.

Daniel 11:5.text: He will strengthen Egypt’s kingdom, and one of the rulers will overpower him and rule; his rule will be a great rule.

Daniel 11:6.text: At the completion of years he will lead them, and the king of Egypt will enter the northern kingdom to make treaties. He will not prevail, for his arm will not establish strength; his arm and that of those traveling with him will grow numb, and he will remain until the appointed hours.

Daniel 11:7.text: A plant from his root will arise on its own, and the king of the north will come against his force with his strength, cause turmoil, and prevail.

Daniel 11:8.text: He will overthrow their gods together with their cast images, and they will carry their crowds, with their precious vessels, silver, and gold, captive to Egypt. There will be a year for the king of the north.

Daniel 11:9.text: He will enter Egypt’s kingdom for days and return to his land,

Daniel 11:10.text: and so will his son. He will be provoked, gather an assembly of a great crowd, and enter against it, sweeping through. He will pass over, return, and be greatly provoked.

Daniel 11:11.text: The king of Egypt will become angry and fight the king of the north, and the assembled force will be handed into his hands.

Daniel 11:12.text: He will take the assembled force, and his heart will be exalted. He will throw many into turmoil and will not be afraid.

Daniel 11:13.text: The king of the north will return and gather a city’s force larger than the first at the completion of a year’s appointed time. He will enter it against him with a great crowd and much money.

Daniel 11:14.text: In those times designs will rise against the king of Egypt. He will rebuild the fallen things of your nation and arise to establish the prophecy, but they will stumble.

Daniel 11:15.text: The king of the north will come, turn his spears, and take the fortified city. The arms of Egypt’s king will stand with his rulers, but he will have no strength to resist him.

Daniel 11:16.text: The one coming against him will act according to his will, and no one will resist before him. He will stand in the country, and everything will be accomplished in his hands.

Daniel 11:17.text: He will set his face to advance all his undertaking by force and make treaties with him. He will give him a daughter of a human to destroy her, but she will not obey and will not remain.

Daniel 11:18.text: He will set his face toward the sea and take many. He will turn back the wrath of their reproach with an oath according to his reproach.

Daniel 11:19.text: He will turn his face to strengthen his country, but stumble, fall, and not be found.

Daniel 11:20.text: From his root a royal plant will arise, a man striking a king’s glory. In the last days he will be shattered, but not in wrath or war.

Daniel 11:21.text: In his place will arise one easily despised, upon whom royal glory will not be bestowed. He will come suddenly; a king will prevail in his allotment.

Daniel 11:22.text: He will shatter the already-shattered arms before him.

Daniel 11:23.text: With the covenant and a people arrayed with him, he will act falsely and act against a strong nation with a very small nation.

Daniel 11:24.text: He will suddenly desolate a city and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will give them plunder, spoils, and money and devise plans against the strong city, but his plans will be in vain.

Daniel 11:25.text: His strength and heart will be stirred against Egypt’s king with a great crowd. Egypt’s king will be provoked to war with an exceedingly strong crowd, but will not stand, because he will devise a design against him.

Daniel 11:26.text: His anxieties will consume him and turn him away. He will pass through and sweep away, and many wounded will fall.

Daniel 11:27.text: Two kings alone will dine together, eat at one table, and speak falsely, but they will not prosper, for completion still awaits its appointed time.

Daniel 11:28.text: He will return to his country with much money, his heart against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his country

Daniel 11:29.text: at the appointed time. He will enter Egypt, but it will not be as the first and the last.

Daniel 11:30.text: Romans will come, drive him out, and rebuke him. He will return, become angry against the holy covenant, act, and return. He will consider them because they abandoned the holy covenant.

Daniel 11:31.text: Arms from him will arise, defile the sanctuary of fear, remove the sacrifice, and establish an abomination of desolation.

Daniel 11:32.text: In sins against the covenant they will defile with a harsh people, but the people who know these things will be strong and act.

Daniel 11:33.text: The thoughtful of the nation will give understanding to many. They will stumble by the sword and grow old in it; in captivity and plunder they will be stained for days.

Daniel 11:34.text: When they are crushed, they will gather a little strength. Many will assemble with them at a city, and many as in an allotment.

Daniel 11:35.text: Some of those who understand will consider how to purify themselves, be selected, and be cleansed until the time of completion, for the time still awaits its hours.

Daniel 11:36.text: The king will act according to his will, become enraged, and be exalted above every god. He will speak extraordinary things against the God of gods and prosper until the wrath is completed, for completion is coming upon him.

Daniel 11:37.text: He will pay no heed to his fathers’ gods or to the desire of a woman, for he will be exalted in everything, and strong nations will be subject to him.

Daniel 11:38.text: He will stir in his place and honor a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, and costly stone. And with the desirable things

Daniel 11:39.text: of cities he will act, and he will come into a strong fortification. With a foreign god, whom he may acknowledge, he will multiply glory, rule over him greatly, and apportion country as a gift.

Daniel 11:40.text: At the hour of completion, Egypt’s king will clash with him. The king of the north will rage against him with chariots, many horses, and many ships, and enter Egypt’s country

Daniel 11:42.text: and in Egypt’s country no one will be saved.

Daniel 11:43.text: He will control the place of gold, the place of silver, and all Egypt’s desirable wealth; Libyans and Ethiopians will be in his multitude.

Daniel 11:44.text: A report from the east and north will disturb him, and he will go out in strong anger and with a sword to wipe out and kill many.

Daniel 11:45.text: Then he will set his tent between the seas and the mountain of the Holy One’s desire. The hour of his completion will come, and no one will help him.”

Daniel 12:1.text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

Daniel 12:2.text: Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.

Daniel 12:3.text: Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.

Daniel 12:4.text: But you, Daniel, cover the commands and seal the book until the time of completion, until the many go mad and the earth is filled with injustice.”

Daniel 12:5.text: I, Daniel, saw two others standing, one on this side of the river and one on the other.

Daniel 12:6.text: I said to the one clothed in fine linen above, “When, then, will the wonders you have told me reach completion, and these things be cleansed?”

Daniel 12:7.text: I heard the one clothed in fine linen above the river’s water say, “Until the time of completion.” He raised his right hand and his left to heaven and swore by God who lives for ever that in a time, times, and half a time would be the completion of the “hands of release” of a holy people, and all these things would be completed.

Daniel 12:8.text: I heard, but did not understand the time from him. I said, “My lord, what is the interpretation of this word, and what do these figures concern?”

Daniel 12:9.text: He said to me, “Go away, Daniel, for the commands are covered and sealed until

Daniel 12:10.text: many are tested and made holy, and sinners sin. None of the sinners will understand, but those who understand will pay attention.

Daniel 12:11.text: From when the sacrifice is removed for all time and preparations are made to set up the abomination of desolation: one thousand two hundred ninety days.

Daniel 12:12.text: Blessed is the one who perseveres and reaches a total of one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.

Daniel 12:13.text: But you, go and rest, for there are still days and hours until completion is fulfilled. You will rest and arise unto your glory at the completion of days.”

Susanna 1:6.text: And judicial cases from other cities came to them.

Susanna 1:7–8.text: These men saw a woman lovely in appearance, the wife of their brother from the sons of Israel, named Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah and wife of Joachim, walking in her husband’s garden in the evening. They desired her

Susanna 1:9.text: and distorted their minds, turning their eyes aside so as not to look toward heaven or remember righteous judgments.

Susanna 1:10–11.text: Both were stricken with desire for her, but neither admitted to the other the evil that possessed them concerning her. The woman herself knew nothing of this matter.

Susanna 1:12.text: As dawn came, they would come, trying to outwit one another in their hurry to see who would appear to her first and speak with her.

Susanna 1:13–14.text: And behold, she was walking as usual. One of the elders had arrived, and behold, the other came. One questioned the other, saying, “Why did you go out so early without taking me?” Then each confessed his anguish to the other.

Susanna 1:19.text: One said to the other, “Let us go to her.” Having agreed, they approached her and tried to force her.

Susanna 1:22.text: The Jewish woman said to them, “I know that if I do this, it means death for me; and if I do not, I will not escape your hands.

Susanna 1:23.text: But it is better for me to fall into your hands without having done it than to sin before the Lord.”

Susanna 1:28.text: The lawless men went back, making threats among themselves and plotting to kill her. They came to the assembly of the city where they were residing, and all the sons of Israel who were there sat together in council.

Susanna 1:29.text: The two elders and judges stood up and said, “Send for Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, who is Joachim’s wife.” They summoned her at once.

Susanna 1:30.text: The woman arrived with her father and mother. Her male and female servants, numbering five hundred, also arrived, together with Susanna’s four children.

Susanna 1:32.text: The lawless men ordered her to be uncovered, so that they might satisfy their desire for her beauty.

Susanna 1:33.text: All her people, and everyone who knew her, wept.

Susanna 1:34.text: The elders and judges stood up and laid their hands on her head.

Susanna 1:35.text: But her heart trusted in the Lord her God. Raising her head, she wept within herself, saying,

Susanna 1:35a.text: “Lord, everlasting God, who knowest all things before they come into being, Thou knowest that I have not done what these lawless men wickedly allege against me.” And the Lord heard her petition.

Susanna 1:36.text: The two elders said, “We were walking in her husband’s garden,

Susanna 1:37.text: and as we went around the course, we saw this woman reclining with a man. We stood and watched them being intimate with one another,

Susanna 1:38.text: and they did not know that we were standing there. Then we said to one another, ‘Let us find out who these people are.’

Susanna 1:39.text: We approached and recognized her, but the young man fled, covered up.

Susanna 1:40.text: We seized her and asked her, ‘Who is the man?’

Susanna 1:41.text: She did not tell us who he was. We testify to these things.” The whole assembly believed them because they were elders and judges of the people.

Susanna 1:44–45.text: And behold, an angel of the Lord was there as she was being led out to perish. As he had been commanded, the angel gave a spirit of understanding to Daniel, who was young.

Susanna 1:48.text: Daniel parted the crowd, stood in their midst, and said, “Are you so foolish, sons of Israel? Have you condemned a daughter of Israel without an inquiry or a clear knowledge of the facts?

Susanna 1:51.text: Now separate them far from one another for me, so that I may examine them.”

Susanna 1:52.text: When they had been separated, Daniel said to the assembly, “Do not now look at the fact that these men are elders and say, ‘They certainly will not lie.’ I will question them according to what occurs to me.” He called one of them, and they brought the elder to the young man. Daniel said to him, “Listen, listen, you who have grown old in evil days! Now your sins have come upon you, the things you formerly did

Susanna 1:53.text: when you were entrusted with hearing and judging cases that bring death: you condemned the innocent and would release the guilty, although the Lord says, ‘You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous.’

Susanna 1:54.text: Now then, under what tree, and in what part of the garden, did you see them together?” The impious man said, “Under a mastic tree.”

Susanna 1:55.text: The young man said, “You have indeed lied against your own soul, for the angel of the Lord will split your soul today.”

Susanna 1:56.text: He moved this man aside and said to bring the other to him. To this man he said, “Why is your offspring corrupted, like Sidon’s and not like Judah’s? Beauty and filthy desire deceived you!

Susanna 1:57.text: This is how you used to treat the daughters of Israel, and they were intimate with you because they were afraid. But a daughter of Judah did not endure bearing your disease in lawlessness.

Susanna 1:58.text: Now then, tell me: under what tree, and in what part of the garden, did you catch them being intimate with one another?” He said, “Under a holm-oak.”

Susanna 1:59.text: Daniel said, “Sinner, the angel of the Lord now stands holding his sword, until the people utterly destroy you both, so that he may saw you apart.”

Susanna 1:60–62.text: The whole assembly cried out over the young man, because from their own mouths he had established that both were admittedly false witnesses. As the law prescribes, they did to them what they had wickedly plotted against their sister. They gagged them, took them out, and threw them into a ravine. Then the angel of the Lord cast fire through their midst. Innocent blood was saved that day.

Susanna 1:63.text: For this reason the young are beloved of Jacob in their simplicity. Let us also be attentive to capable young sons, for the young will be devout, and a spirit of knowledge and understanding will be in them for ever and ever.

Bel and Dragon 1:1.text: From the prophecy of Habakkuk, son of Joshua, of the tribe of Levi.

Bel and Dragon 1:2.text: There was a certain priest named Daniel, son of Abal, a companion of the king of Babylon.

Bel and Dragon 1:3.text: There was an idol, Bel, whom the Babylonians revered. Each day twelve artabas of fine flour, four sheep, and six metretas of oil were expended for him.

Bel and Dragon 1:4.text: The king revered him and went each day to bow before him, but Daniel prayed to the Lord.

Bel and Dragon 1:5.text: The king said to Daniel, “Why do you not bow before Bel?” Daniel said to the king, “I revere no one except the Lord God, who created heaven and earth and has lordship over all flesh.”

Bel and Dragon 1:6.text: The king said to him, “Is this one, then, not a god? Do you not see how much is spent on him every day?”

Bel and Dragon 1:7.text: Daniel said to him, “Certainly not! Let no one deceive you. This one is clay on the inside and bronze on the outside. I swear to you by the Lord, the God of gods, that this one has never eaten anything.”

Bel and Dragon 1:8.text: The king became angry, called those in charge of the temple, and said to them, “Show who eats what is prepared for Bel. Otherwise, either you will die or Daniel, who claims that these things are not eaten by him.” They said, “Bel himself is the one who eats them.”

Bel and Dragon 1:9.text: Daniel said to the king, “Let it be so. If I do not demonstrate that Bel is not the one who eats these things, I and all my people will die.” Bel had seventy priests, apart from their wives and children.

Bel and Dragon 1:10.text: They brought the king into the idol-temple.

Bel and Dragon 1:11.text: The food was set out before the king and Daniel. Mixed wine was brought in and placed before Bel. Daniel said, “You yourself see that these things are laid out, O king. So seal the locks of the temple yourself when it has been closed.”

Bel and Dragon 1:14.text: Daniel ordered his people to put everyone out of the temple and sprinkle the whole temple with ashes, without anyone outside his own group knowing. Then he ordered the temple to be sealed with the king’s ring and the rings of certain distinguished priests. It was done that way.

Bel and Dragon 1:15–17.text: The next day they came to the place. Meanwhile, Bel’s priests had entered through secret doors, eaten everything laid before Bel, and drunk all the wine. Daniel said, “Men who are priests, inspect your seals to see whether they remain. And you, O king, examine whether anything has turned out contrary to what you expected.” They found the seal as it had been, and removed the seal.

Bel and Dragon 1:18.text: They opened the doors and saw that everything set out had been consumed and the tables were empty. The king rejoiced and said to Daniel, “Bel is great, and there is no deceit in him.”

Bel and Dragon 1:19.text: Daniel laughed heartily and said to the king, “Come, see the priests’ deceit.” Daniel said, “O king, whose footprints are these?”

Bel and Dragon 1:20.text: The king said, “Those of men, women, and children.”

Bel and Dragon 1:21.text: He went to the house where the priests were staying and found Bel’s food and the wine. Daniel showed the king the secret doors through which the priests would enter and consume what was laid before Bel.

Bel and Dragon 1:22.text: The king brought them out of Bel’s temple and handed them over to Daniel. He gave Daniel the expenditure allocated to Bel, and destroyed Bel.

Bel and Dragon 1:23.text: There was a dragon in the same place, and the Babylonians revered it.

Bel and Dragon 1:24.text: The king said to Daniel, “Will you say that this one is bronze too? Behold, it lives, eats, and drinks. Bow before it.”

Bel and Dragon 1:25.text: Daniel said, “O king, give me authority, and I will kill the dragon without iron or a rod.”

Bel and Dragon 1:26.text: The king consented and said to him, “It is granted to you.”

Bel and Dragon 1:27.text: Daniel took thirty minas of pitch, together with fat and hair, boiled them together, made a cake, and threw it into the dragon’s mouth. It ate and burst apart. He showed it to the king, saying, “Are these not the things you revere, O king?”

Bel and Dragon 1:28.text: All the people from the country gathered against Daniel and said, “The king has become a Jew! He has destroyed Bel and killed the dragon.”

Bel and Dragon 1:30.text: The king saw that the crowd of the country had gathered against him. He called his companions and said, “I hand Daniel over to destruction.”

Bel and Dragon 1:31–32.text: There was a pit in which seven lions were kept. Those who plotted against the king were handed over to them, and each day two bodies of people condemned to death were supplied to them. The crowds threw Daniel into that pit so that he would be devoured and would not even receive burial. Daniel was in the pit for six days.

Bel and Dragon 1:33.text: On the sixth day, Habakkuk had bread crumbled in a trough with stew, and a jar of mixed wine. He was going into the field to the reapers.

Bel and Dragon 1:34.text: An angel of the Lord spoke to Habakkuk, saying, “Thus says the Lord God to you: ‘Take the meal you have to Daniel in the lions’ pit in Babylon.’”

Bel and Dragon 1:35.text: Habakkuk said, “Lord God, I have not seen Babylon, and I do not know where the pit is.”

Bel and Dragon 1:36.text: The angel of the Lord took Habakkuk by the hair of his head and set him above the pit in Babylon.

Bel and Dragon 1:37.text: Habakkuk said to Daniel, “Get up and eat the meal that the Lord God has sent you.”

Bel and Dragon 1:38.text: Daniel said, “For the Lord God has remembered me, He who does not abandon those who love Him.”

Bel and Dragon 1:39.text: Daniel ate. The angel of the Lord returned Habakkuk to the place from which he had taken him on that same day. And the Lord God remembered Daniel.

Bel and Dragon 1:40.text: After these things the king went out mourning Daniel. He bent down into the pit and saw him sitting there.

Bel and Dragon 1:41.text: The king cried aloud and said, “The Lord God is great, and there is no other besides Him.”

Bel and Dragon 1:42.text: The king brought Daniel out of the pit. Before Daniel’s eyes he threw into the pit those responsible for his destruction, and they were devoured.

Deuteronomy 4:27.text: And the Lord shall scatter you among all the nations, and you shall be left few in number among the nations whither the Lord shall bring you.

Deuteronomy 4:28.text: And there you shall serve other gods, the works of men’s hands, wood and stone, which shall neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

Deuteronomy 4:29.text: And there you shall seek the Lord your God, and shall find Him, when you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul, in your distress.

Deuteronomy 4:30.text: And all these things shall find you in the latter days, and you shall return unto the Lord your God, and hearken unto His voice.

Deuteronomy 4:31.text: For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not forsake you, neither will He destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which He sware unto them.

Deuteronomy 28:62.text: And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

Deuteronomy 28:63.text: And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.

Deuteronomy 28:64.text: And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.

Deuteronomy 32:39.text: See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.

Esther 8:1.text: On that very day King Artaxerxes gave Esther everything that belonged to Haman the slanderer. Mordecai was summoned by the king, for Esther had explained that he was related to her.

Esther 8:2.text: The king took the signet ring he had removed from Haman and gave it to Mordecai. Esther appointed Mordecai over all Haman’s possessions.

Esther 8:3.text: She spoke to the king again, fell at his feet, and asked him to remove Haman’s wickedness and everything he had done to the Jews.

Esther 8:4.text: The king extended the golden scepter to Esther, and Esther rose to stand before the king.

Esther 8:5.text: Esther said, “If it seems good to you, and I have found favor, let an order be sent to reverse the letters sent out by Haman, which were written for the destruction of the Jews in your kingdom.

Esther 8:6.text: For how shall I be able to see the affliction of my people? How shall I be able to survive the destruction of my homeland?”

Esther 8:7.text: The king said to Esther, “If I have given and granted you all Haman’s possessions, and have hung him on a tree because he raised his hands against the Jews, what more do you seek?

Genesis 41:1.text: And after two full years Pharaoh dreamed a dream. He thought he was standing beside the river.

Genesis 41:2.text: And behold, as though from the river there came up seven cows, fair in appearance and choice in flesh, and they grazed among the reeds.

Genesis 41:3.text: And seven other cows came up after them from the river, ugly in appearance and lean in flesh, and they grazed beside the cows upon the riverbank.

Genesis 41:4.text: And the seven cows which were ugly and lean in flesh devoured the seven cows which were fair in appearance and choice. And Pharaoh awoke.

Genesis 41:5.text: And he dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, choice and good.

Genesis 41:6.text: And seven other ears sprouted after them, thin and blighted by the wind.

Genesis 41:7.text: And the seven thin ears, blighted by the wind, swallowed the seven choice and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and it was a dream.

Genesis 41:8.text: And morning came, and his soul was troubled; and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them the dream, and there was none to explain it to Pharaoh.

Genesis 41:9.text: And the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my offence today.

Genesis 41:10.text: “Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put us in custody in the house of the chief cook, me and the chief baker.

Genesis 41:11.text: “And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; each of us saw his own dream.

Genesis 41:12.text: “And a young Hebrew servant of the chief cook was with us, and we told him, and he interpreted to us.

Genesis 41:13.text: “And as he interpreted to us, so it happened: I was restored to my office, and he was hanged.”

Genesis 41:14.text: And Pharaoh sent and called Joseph; and they brought him out of the fortress, and shaved him, and changed his garments; and he came to Pharaoh.

Genesis 41:15.text: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is none to interpret it; but I have heard it said concerning you, that when you hear dreams, you can interpret them.”

Genesis 41:16.text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “Without God, no answer bringing deliverance shall be given to Pharaoh.”

Genesis 41:25.text: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh’s dream is one. God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.

Genesis 41:26.text: “The seven fair cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. Pharaoh’s dream is one.

Genesis 41:27.text: “And the seven lean cows which came up after them are seven years; and the seven thin ears, blighted by the wind, shall be seven years of famine.

Genesis 41:28.text: “And this is the word which I have spoken to Pharaoh: God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.

Genesis 41:29.text: “Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming in all the land of Egypt.

Genesis 41:30.text: “And seven years of famine shall come after them, and they shall forget the plenty in all the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land.

Genesis 41:31.text: “And the abundance shall not be known in the land because of the famine which shall follow, for it shall be exceedingly severe.

Genesis 41:32.text: “And as for Pharaoh’s dream being repeated twice, it is because the word from God shall be true, and God shall hasten to do it.

Job 12:2.text: “So you are the people! Surely wisdom will die with you!

Job 12:3.text: I too have a heart like yours.

Job 12:4.text: For a righteous and blameless man became an object of mockery.

Job 12:5.text: For at an appointed time he was prepared to fall beneath others, and for his houses to be plundered by the lawless.

Job 12:6.text: But indeed, let no wicked person trust that he will be innocent, nor those who provoke the Lord suppose that there will be no examination of them.

Job 12:7.text: But ask the four-footed animals, to see whether they will tell you, and the birds of heaven, to see whether they will report to you.

Job 12:8.text: Speak fully to the earth, to see whether it will tell you; and the fish of the sea will explain to you.

Job 12:9.text: Who among all these did not know that the Lord’s hand made these things?

Job 12:10.text: Is not the life of all living things in His hand, and the breath of every human being?

Job 12:11.text: For the ear discerns words, and the throat tastes food.

Job 12:12.text: In much time is wisdom, and in a long life knowledge.

Job 12:13.text: With Him are wisdom and power; to Him belong counsel and understanding.

Job 12:14.text: If He throws down, who will build? If He shuts people in, who will open?

Job 12:15.text: If He restrains water, He will dry the earth; if He lets it loose, He destroys it by overturning it.

Job 12:16.text: With Him are might and strength; to Him belong knowledge and understanding.

Job 12:17.text: He leads counselors away captive and throws the earth’s judges into confusion.

Job 12:18.text: He seats kings on thrones and bound their waists with a belt.

Job 12:19.text: He sends priests away captive and overthrows the earth’s rulers.

Job 12:20.text: He changes the lips of the faithful and knows the elders’ understanding.

Job 12:21.text: He pours dishonor upon rulers and heals the lowly.

Job 12:22.text: He uncovers deep things from darkness and brings death’s shadow into light.

Job 12:23.text: He leads nations astray and destroys them; He lays nations low and guides them.

Job 12:24.text: He changes the hearts of the earth’s rulers and leads them astray on a road they did not know.

Job 12:25.text: May they grope in darkness and not light; may they wander like one who is drunk.

Psalms 82:1.text: A song of a psalm for Asaph.

Psalms 82:2.text: God, who will be likened unto Thee? Do not be silent or remain quiet, God.

Psalms 82:3.text: For behold, Thine enemies made an uproar, and those who hate Thee lifted their head.

Psalms 82:4.text: Against Thy people they cunningly devised a plan, and they took counsel against Thy holy ones.

Psalms 82:5.text: They said, “Come, let us destroy them from being a nation, and Israel’s name shall certainly be remembered no more.”

Psalms 82:6.text: For they took counsel together in concord; against Thee they made a covenant—

Psalms 82:7.text: the dwellings of the Idumeans, and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarenes,

Psalms 82:8.text: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, and foreigners with those who inhabit Tyre.

Psalms 82:9.text: For Asshur too came alongside them; they became a support for the sons of Lot. Diapsalma.

Psalms 82:10.text: Do to them as to Midian and Sisera, as with Jabin at the torrent Kishon,

Psalms 82:11.text: they were destroyed at En-dor and became like dung for the earth.

Psalms 82:12.text: Make their rulers like Oreb and Zeeb, and Zebah and Zalmunna—all their rulers,

Psalms 82:13.text: who said, “Let us inherit for ourselves the sanctuary of God.”

Psalms 82:14.text: My God, make them like a wheel, like straw before the wind.

Psalms 82:15.text: Like fire that will burn through a woodland, as though a flame should burn up mountains,

Psalms 82:16.text: so Thou wilt pursue them with Thy storm and trouble them in Thy wrath.

Psalms 82:17.text: Fill their faces with dishonor, and they will seek Thy name, Lord.

Psalms 82:18.text: Let them be ashamed and troubled for an age of an age; let them be abashed and perish,

Psalms 82:19.text: and let them know that Thy name is Lord; Thou alone art Most High over all the earth.

Psalms 97:1.text: A psalm of David. Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done wonders. His right hand and His holy arm won salvation for Him.

Psalms 97:2.text: The Lord made His salvation known; before the nations He revealed His righteousness.

Psalms 97:3.text: He remembered His mercy to Jacob and His truth to the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God.

Psalms 97:4.text: Shout to God, all the earth; sing and exult and make music.

Psalms 97:5.text: Make music to the Lord with a lyre, with a lyre and the sound of a psalm.

Psalms 97:6.text: With hammered trumpets and the sound of a horn trumpet, shout before the King, the Lord.

Psalms 97:7.text: Let the sea be shaken, and all that fills it, the inhabited world and those who dwell in it.

Psalms 97:8.text: Rivers will clap their hands together; the mountains will exult,

Psalms 97:9.text: for He has come to judge the earth. He will judge the inhabited world with righteousness and peoples with uprightness.

Psalms 102:19.text: The Lord prepared His throne in heaven, and His kingdom has dominion over all.

Psalms 102:20.text: Bless the Lord, all His angels, mighty in strength, doing His word, so as to hear the voice of His words.

Psalms 102:21.text: Bless the Lord, all His powers, His ministers who do His will.

Psalms 102:22.text: Bless the Lord, all His works, in every place of His dominion. Bless the Lord, my soul.

Psalms 103:3.text: He roofs His upper chambers in waters, makes clouds His means of ascent, and walks on the wings of winds.

Psalms 103:4.text: He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a burning fire.

Psalms 103:5.text: He founded the earth on its stability; it will not be tilted for an age of ages.

Psalms 103:6.text: The deep is His covering like a garment; waters will stand upon the mountains.

Psalms 103:7.text: At Thy rebuke they will flee; at the voice of Thy thunder they will become afraid.

Psalms 103:8.text: Mountains rise and plains descend to the place Thou didst found for them.

Psalms 103:9.text: Thou didst set a boundary they will not pass, nor will they return to cover the earth.

Psalms 103:10.text: He sends springs into the ravines; waters will pass between the mountains.

Psalms 103:11.text: They give drink to all the beasts of the field; wild donkeys will receive it for their thirst.

Psalms 103:12.text: Upon them the birds of heaven will nest; from among the rocks they will give voice.

Psalms 103:13.text: He waters mountains from His upper chambers; the earth will be filled with the fruit of Thy works.

Psalms 103:14.text: He makes grass spring up for livestock and green plants for the service of humans, to bring bread out of the earth;

Psalms 133:1.text: A song of the ascents. Behold, bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.

Psalms 133:2.text: By night lift your hands toward the holy places and bless the Lord.

Psalms 133:3.text: The Lord will bless you from Zion, who made heaven and earth.

Psalms 134:1.text: Hallelujah! Praise the Lord’s name; praise the Lord, slaves,

Psalms 134:2.text: you who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of our God’s house.

Psalms 134:3.text: Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; make music to His name, for it is beautiful.

Psalms 134:4.text: For the Lord chose Jacob for Himself, Israel as His special possession.

Psalms 134:5.text: For I knew that the Lord is great, and our Lord is above all the gods.

Psalms 134:6.text: Everything the Lord willed, He did, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the deeps.

Psalms 134:7.text: He brings clouds up from the earth’s extremity; He made lightning for rain; He brings winds out of His treasuries.

Psalms 134:15.text: The nations’ idols are silver and gold, works of human hands.

Psalms 134:16.text: They have a mouth but will not speak; they have eyes but will not see.

Psalms 134:17.text: They have ears but will not listen; they have noses but will not smell; they have hands but will not touch; they have feet but will not walk; they will not sound in their throat, for there is no breath in their mouth.

Psalms 134:18.text: May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.

Psalms 134:19.text: House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.

Psalms 134:20.text: House of Levi, bless the Lord; you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord.

Psalms 134:21.text: Blessed be the Lord from Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem.

Psalms 135:1.text: Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for He is kind; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:2.text: Give thanks to the God of gods; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:3.text: Give thanks to the Lord of lords; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:4.text: To Him who alone does great wonders; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:5.text: To Him who made the heavens with understanding; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:6.text: To Him who made the earth firm upon the waters; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:7.text: To Him who alone made great lights; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:8.text: the sun for authority over the day; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 135:9.text: the moon and stars for authority over the night; for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 138:1.text: For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.

Psalms 138:2.text: Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.

Psalms 138:3.text: Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.

Psalms 138:4.text: For there is no word on my tongue,

Psalms 138:5.text: behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.

Psalms 138:11.text: And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”

Psalms 138:12.text: For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.

Psalms 146:1.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; may praise be pleasing to our God.

Psalms 146:2.text: The Lord builds Jerusalem, and He will gather the dispersed of Israel.

Psalms 146:3.text: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their fractures.

Psalms 146:4.text: He numbers multitudes of stars and calls them all by names.

Psalms 146:5.text: Great is our Lord, and great is His strength; His understanding is beyond number.

Psalms 146:6.text: The Lord takes up the meek, but brings sinners low to the ground.

Psalms 146:7.text: Begin singing to the Lord with thanksgiving; make music to our God with a lyre,

Psalms 146:8.text: who clothes heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains and green growth for the service of humans,

Psalms 146:9.text: who gives the cattle their food and to the young ravens who call upon Him.

Psalms 146:10.text: He will not delight in the horse’s might, nor does He take pleasure in a man’s shins.

Psalms 146:11.text: The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him and in those who hope in His mercy.

Psalms 147:1.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Commend the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.

Psalms 147:2.text: For He strengthened the bars of your gates; He blessed your children within you.

Psalms 147:3.text: He makes your borders peaceful and fills you with the finest wheat.

Psalms 147:4.text: He sends His oracle to the earth; His word will run swiftly,

Psalms 147:5.text: of Him who gives snow like wool, who sprinkles mist like ashes,

Psalms 147:6.text: who casts His ice like morsels; who will withstand His cold?

Psalms 147:7.text: He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

Psalms 147:8.text: He declares His word to Jacob, His ordinances and judgments to Israel.

Psalms 147:9.text: He did not do so for any nation, and He did not disclose His judgments to them.

Psalms 148:1.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places.

Psalms 148:2.text: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers.

Psalms 148:3.text: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.

Psalms 148:4.text: Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.

Psalms 148:5.text: Let them praise the Lord’s name, for He spoke, and they came to be; He commanded, and they were created.

Psalms 148:6.text: He established them for the age and for the age of the age; He set a command, and it will not pass away.

Psalms 148:7.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,

Psalms 148:8.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

Psalms 148:9.text: mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars,

Psalms 148:10.text: wild animals and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds,

Psalms 148:11.text: kings of the earth and all peoples, rulers and all judges of the earth,

Psalms 148:12.text: young men and young women, old people with younger people.

Psalms 148:13.text: Let them praise the Lord’s name, for His name alone was exalted; His praise is over earth and heaven.

Psalms 148:14.text: He will raise a horn of His people— a hymn for all His holy ones, for the children of Israel, a people drawing near to Him.

Psalms 150:1.text: Hallelujah. Praise God among His holy ones; praise Him in the firmament of His power.

Psalms 150:2.text: Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the abundance of His greatness.

Sirach 3:28.text: There is no healing for a proud person’s calamity, for a plant of wickedness has taken root in him.

Sirach 3:29.text: An understanding heart will consider a proverb, and a listening ear is the desire of a wise person.

Sirach 3:30.text: Water will extinguish a blazing fire, and almsgiving will atone for sins.

Sirach 3:31.text: The one who repays favors takes thought for what comes afterward, and at the time of his fall he will find support.
